X.note: Drops 'translucentes' ('some gems'); 'lexiva' as 'lees'; otherwise close, apparatus kept.

Y.note: Omits footnote and apparatus; completes truncated last sentence with footnote's 'shortest line between two points'.

X.note: Verse garbled ('Then I shall be reborn to my brothers'); speaker labels 'I:/You:'; omits 'vadosa' and margin 'Sacra fana nocte'.

Y.note: Commentary errors: 'grieving' for seeking, 'plow' for chariot, 'father who created them' for Creon; adds 'other gods'.

X.note: Omits Melli and margin notes; 'these [camels]' use tridents; 'violating the established custom' misreads 'ut alter alterum non videat'.

Y.note: Heavily garbled: 'land of black honey', 'They lack four feet... this makes them unjust', 'by means of their blackness'.

X.note: 'which at first was entirely good' misreads 'in primis parentibus tota erat'; 'sensuality to desire' should be 'to will'.

Y.note: 'peremptores' rendered 'purchasers' (should be destroyers), twice; 'brute beasts within man'; adds 'holy'.

X.note: Never names the boar; 'goats' for its young; 'has caused no damage' reverses 'pepercit nullis' (spared nothing).

Y.note: 'bringing generous litters of piglets' misreads 'generosa flagella... corrumpere'; 'unlike what is usual' reverses 'more solito'.

X.note: Complete; 'Jude' for Thaddeus is an acceptable identification.

Y.note: Complete and accurate litany.

X.note: Minor slips: 'Davernia' for Deventer, 'translated into Latin verse' by Rimitius (verse not in source).

Y.note: 'On instructing the Youth' for De instruendis aciebus; 'Davenport'; 'Tables' for fables; 'Anterior Days'.

X.note: Largely incoherent on abbreviated source; meta-preamble added; e.g. 'friction of fire' for extinctio ignis, first-person 'I know' throughout.

Y.note: Degenerates into endless repetition 'What is it that is known?'; most of the page absent.

X.note: Reverses negation: 'surely all these people did not know what a solecism was' (source: they were not ignorant).

Y.note: Same negation reversal; 'Quadrigarius to be future', 'He did not say it was a solecism, but' garble the grammatical argument.

X.note: 'ninety-five propositions' (source: 59); 'germana' as 'German translation'; omits 'in Bithynia'.

Y.note: 'ninety-five propositions' (source: nouem et quinquaginta = 59); 'one German' misreads 'germana'.

X.note: 'you are the one who sows dung' (metere = reap); 'conspire against' for coniurare (conjure).

Y.note: 'measuring dung' for reaping; 'My dear foot' for Füechß (fox).

X.note: Skips donkey/horse/sheep dung, pig dung, and the fresh vs year-old manure passage; jumps to physicians' dwellings.

Y.note: 'Salt is mixed' for Saladius (Palladius); 'physicians and apothecaries' for physicians of consumptives; 'dry appetites'.

X.note: Omits 'ante annos undeviginti' (19 years ago); garbles the sentence on the last proposition limiting generality.

Y.note: 'twenty-one years ago' (source: nineteen); third person 'he came upon' for 'incidi'.

X.note: 'that it might move in a deficient manner' reverses 'indeficienter'; 'immaterial' for immobilis.

Y.note: Reverses key claim: 'motion of the heavens becomes deficient and is open to every irregularity'; 'first lion's eighth'.

X.note: Corrupt source; long stretch copied as Latin words strung with 'as' ('as stra as fiam as Lin...').

Y.note: Corrupt source rendered into largely invented sense ('in a blazing fire, in a noisy road').

X.note: 'licet mane sumendum' as 'taken with caution' (should be: in the morning); 'Nile is also watered'.

Y.note: Reverses negation: 'we will cite the agreement of various physicists' (source: we will not).

X.note: 'Book V' for Martial book VI; 'becoming senile' for caecutientes (half-blind).

Y.note: 'The terebinth is more foolish' inverts comparison; 'deaf' for caecus; 'fifth book' for VI.

X.note: 'present events have aided' — source: the gods, present, brought aid.

Y.note: 'carried out by you, citizens' (source: a me, by me); 'He had stripped your heads' wrong subject.

X.note: 'Do not grant me death' for minitaris; omits 'cui nec satis est quod est'; 'torture your pleasures' garbles libidines te torquent.

Y.note: 'Nor do I allow injury to weaken my enemies'; 'Your lusts are concealed'; 'Let me not prevent you from sighing'.

X.note: Accurate throughout.

Y.note: 'To be siderated'; 'In genus, secondly'; 'by whom such actions are begun' misreads 'inita'.
